name: What should be included in a custom kitchen design proposal?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a custom kitchen design proposal?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a custom kitchen design proposal?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom kitchen design proposal should be detailed enough to show exactly what is being designed, built, and excluded. It should include the project scope, layout plan, cabinetry specifications, countertop material assumptions, appliance allowances, lighting scope, plumbing and electrical scope, finish carpentry, and any structural work. The proposal should also identify who handles permits, inspections, demolition, trash removal, and site protection. A schedule matters too, especially for Los Angeles projects where cabinet lead times and permit approvals can affect the overall timeline. Homeowners should look for clear allowances rather than vague estimates, because a bid that seems low may simply be missing important items. The proposal should also note change-order procedures, payment milestones, and what happens if hidden conditions are found after demolition. If these details are missing, the project is harder to manage and more likely to run over budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: A strong custom kitchen proposal should include scope, drawings, material allowances, cabinetry details, appliance assumptions, timeline, exclusions, and permit responsibilities. Without those items, it is hard to compare bids accurately or control cost changes later.
